synopsis: ISO 18497-4:2024 covers verification methods and validation principles for partially automated, semi-autonomous and autonomous agricultural machinery, including braking, steering, and person or obstacle detection tests; the agricultural family is a close analogue to the heavy off-road collision-mitigation function studied [f1711, f7190]. The 2024 Parts 1–4 were published in July 2024, with Parts 1, 2 and 4 reported as replacing ISO 18497:2018 [f7187, f9763]. Part 4 explicitly lists simulation alongside inspection, measurement, test and analysis, and Annex C provides test objects for simulation, making it the closest off-road standard support for simulation found in the review [f9764, f5276, f5277]. This supports simulation as one method among several, not an established field-test replacement: the research found neither authorization to replace any share of field tests nor an agricultural simulation-based acceptance case [f10294, f15288, f1881]. For planning, important gaps remain: the standard supplies no statistical acceptance target, and the review did not identify a minimum-method table [f324, f9765].
